title: Comparison of vertex and edge actions on marked simplicial sets
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and marked simplicial sets and coordinatewise product markings of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Let $A$ be a small simplicial set, let $Y=(U,E_Y)$ and $X=(V,E_X)$ be small marked simplicial sets, and let $\mu:A^\sharp\times Y\to X$ be a marked simplicial map, where $A^\sharp$ marks every edge of $A$. Let $Z$ be any small quasicategory and $h:V\to Z$ a simplicial map taking $E_X$ to equivalences. For any edge $e:\Delta^1\to U$ and any edge $g:\Delta^1\to A$, put $g^*e=\mu\circ(g,e):\Delta^1\to V$. For a vertex $a\in A_0$, put $a^*e=\mu\circ(\operatorname{const}_a,e)$. Then $h(g^*e)$ is an equivalence in $Z$ if and only if $h(g(0)^*e)$ is an equivalence in $Z$. In particular, if $h(a^*e)$ is an equivalence for every vertex $a$ of $A$, then $h(g^*e)$ is an equivalence for every edge $g$ of $A$. No marking hypothesis is made on $e$, and no Kan hypothesis is made on $A,U$ or $V$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed p.176, last paragraph: comparison with a degenerate acting edge by a simplicial homotopy, formulated for an arbitrary marked action map. Read online 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this marked simplicial result; HTT is not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Write $a_0=g(0)$ and $y_1=e(1)$. The function $m:\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}$, $m(r,t)=\min(r,t)$, is order preserving. In degree $n$, it sends a pair of monotone maps $r,t:[n]\to[1]$ to the monotone map $i\mapsto\min(r(i),t(i))$; this commutes with precomposition by every simplicial operator. It therefore defines $m:\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$. Define the underlying simplicial map $H(r,t)=\mu(g(m(r,t)),e(t))$. Its restrictions at $r=0$ and $r=1$ are respectively $a_0^*e$ and $g^*e$. Thus $H$ is an explicit simplicial homotopy comparing the vertex action with the edge action; no fillers in $A,U$ or $V$ are used.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed p.176, final paragraph; explicit minimum homotopy and one of its triangular restrictions.

proof.text: On the side $t=1$ of this homotopy, $H(r,1)=\mu(g(r),\operatorname{const}_{y_1}(r))$. The edge $g$ is marked in $A^\sharp$ and the constant edge at $y_1$ is degenerate, hence marked in $Y$. The coordinatewise product marking makes their pair marked in $A^\sharp\times Y$. Since $\mu$ is a marked map, its image $v=\mu\circ(g,\operatorname{const}_{y_1})$ belongs to $E_X$. The hypothesis on $h$ therefore makes $h(v)$ an equivalence in $Z$. This marking argument uses no marking of $e$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed p.176, final paragraph; explicit minimum homotopy and one of its triangular restrictions.

proof.text: The two monotone maps $\alpha,\beta:[2]\to[1]$ given by $\alpha=(0,0,1)$ and $\beta=(0,1,1)$ give a simplicial map $j=(\alpha,\beta):\Delta^2\to\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$. On its image, $m(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha$. The three edges $01,12,02$ of $Hj$ are consequently $a_0^*e$, $v$, and $g^*e$, respectively. Apply $h$ to this actual $2$-simplex. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], its edges give the relation $[h(v)]\,[h(a_0^*e)]=[h(g^*e)]$ in the ordinary category $hZ$, and an edge of $Z$ is an equivalence precisely when its component class is invertible. By step 2 the class $[h(v)]$ has an inverse. If $[h(a_0^*e)]$ is invertible, the displayed composite is invertible, with inverse $[h(a_0^*e)]^{-1}[h(v)]^{-1}$. Conversely, if $[h(g^*e)]$ is invertible, then $[h(a_0^*e)]=[h(v)]^{-1}[h(g^*e)]$ is invertible. This proves the claimed if and only if.

source.place: Remarks 4.6.8.10 and 4.6.8.14; apply the existing mapping-composition statement to the explicit triangular restriction of the HTT interval homotopy.

proof.text: If $h(a^*e)$ is an equivalence for every vertex $a$ of $A$, apply this assumption to the initial vertex $a=g(0)$ of any edge $g$ and use step 3. This gives $h(g^*e)$ an equivalence for every edge $g$. If $A$ has no vertices, it has no edges, so both universal assertions are vacuous.
